title: The Mirrors of the Serving Women
theme: Bezalel makes the bronze altar, the bronze basin from the mirrors of the women who served at the tent's entrance, and the courtyard with its hangings and gate. The chapter ends with a careful accounting of the gold, silver and bronze given, including the ransom silver of every counted Israelite.

language.note: Ancient mirrors were polished bronze. Women gave up these personal and valued possessions to make the basin where priests washed. Instruments for looking at oneself became instruments for cleansing before God.

The women 'who served' at the entrance. The verb is used for military service and for the Levites' service at the tabernacle (Numbers 4:23; 8:24). Women had an organized ministry at the tent of meeting (compare 1 Samuel 2:22).
From paqad, 'to count, appoint.' The inventory is made by Ithamar, Aaron's son, at Moses' command. God's work is handled with accountability and transparency.
Literally a 'split,' half a shekel. It was the ransom paid by each of 603,550 counted men (30:13). The silver bases that held the tabernacle up were made from these ransom payments.

usage.note: Paul takes care that no one should blame him in handling the gift, aiming at what is honorable before God and men.
Anna the prophetess did not depart from the temple, worshiping with fasting and prayer night and day.
Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD? He who has clean hands and a pure heart.

context.setting: Construction continues with the courtyard items, repeating 27:1-19 and 30:17-21. Then comes an inventory (v21-31), unusual in ancient texts, listing about a ton of gold, nearly four tons of silver and over two and a half tons of bronze by common estimates. The priestly garments follow in chapter 39.

flow.label: The bronze altar
flow.note: He makes the altar of burnt offering of acacia overlaid with bronze, with horns, utensils, grating, rings and poles.

flow.label: The basin
flow.note: He makes the bronze basin and its stand from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

flow.label: The courtyard
flow.note: He makes the linen hangings, pillars, bases and hooks for the court, and the embroidered screen for the gate.

flow.label: The accounting
flow.note: The Levites under Ithamar record the materials: gold from the wave offering, silver from the census ransom of 603,550 men for bases and hooks, and bronze for the altar, bases and pegs.

tier1.note: The altar and court are built according to the instructions.
The half-shekel ransom collected at the census is used for the tabernacle's silver.
The census in Numbers records the same total of 603,550 men.

tier2.note: Women served at the entrance of the tent of meeting in Eli's day too.
Ithamar oversees the Gershonites and Merarites who carry the tabernacle's structure.
Paul ensures honest handling of the collection.

tier3.note: James compares hearing the word without doing it to looking in a mirror and forgetting. These women turned mirrors into a means of cleansing.
Let your adorning be the inner beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit.
The tabernacle stood on ransom silver; believers stand on a ransom paid not with silver but Christ's blood.

voices.name: Matthew Henry
voices.view: Henry admires the women who gave their mirrors, which ministered to their vanity, to make a laver for cleansing. He sees it as a picture of devotion: turning what served self into something that serves God.

translations.kjv: And he made the laver of brass, and the foot of it of brass, of the lookingglasses of the women assembling, which assembled at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.

renderings.text: from the mirrors of the ministering women who ministered
from the mirrors of the women who served

translations.note: KJV's 'assembling' understates the Hebrew tsava, which means organized service. 'Brass' in the KJV is bronze; brass as we know it was not used then.

translations.kjv: This is the sum of the tabernacle, even of the tabernacle of testimony, as it was counted, according to the commandment of Moses, for the service of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar, son to Aaron the priest.

renderings.text: These are the records of the tabernacle
These are the amounts of the materials used

translations.note: The Hebrew pequdim means 'things counted.' The phrase 'tabernacle of the testimony' links the dwelling to the tablets it would house.

steps.gospel: The silver bases that held up the tabernacle were made from ransom money, half a shekel from every counted Israelite. God's dwelling literally stood on redemption. Believers are built into God's dwelling on the same foundation: not silver but the precious blood of Christ. And the women's mirrors became the basin for cleansing, a reminder that we do not need a better look at ourselves but washing from God, which Christ provides.
application: Give God what is personal and precious, not only what is surplus.
Handle gifts for God's work with transparency and careful records.
Value and honor every kind of service in God's house, including what is often unnoticed.
Stand on Christ's ransom as the foundation of your place among God's people.

misapplications.claim: Concern for accounting and records is unspiritual.
misapplications.correction: God's tabernacle includes a detailed financial record (v21-31), made by a priest at Moses' command. Faithfulness includes good stewardship.

misapplications.claim: The women at the entrance were merely bystanders.
misapplications.correction: The verb tsava describes organized service, used for the Levites' work. They had a recognized role at the tent of meeting.

contrasts.note: Objects of personal appearance became tools of holiness.
The materials' value rises toward the Most Holy Place.
The census payment became the tabernacle's footing.

features.label: An ancient audit
features.note: Detailed weights of gold, silver and bronze are rare in ancient building accounts and show concern for integrity.

features.label: Ithamar's role
features.note: Aaron's son appears in a supervisory role that he will continue in Numbers.

features.label: The basin's material
features.note: Chapter 30 did not say where the basin's bronze came from. Only here do we learn it was the women's mirrors.

steps.summary: Exodus 38 completes the courtyard: the bronze altar, the basin made from the mirrors of serving women, and the hangings and gate. A careful inventory accounts for every precious metal, including the ransom silver that formed the tabernacle's foundation. Devotion, integrity and redemption run through the chapter.

metaArc.book: Chapter 38 completes the structures of the tabernacle complex and closes with an accounting, leading to the priestly garments (chapter 39) and the final assembly (chapter 40).
metaArc.redemptive: This belongs to Redemption: God's dwelling stands on ransom, pointing to the church founded on Christ's redeeming blood.
